defect.description: The backward-incompatible crash: kwargs.pop('method', form.method).upper() raises AttributeError when a caller passes method=None explicitly, which used to work (Request turns a None method into GET); the change should treat None like a missing method.

review_items: src/forms.py:43 important - method=None explicit causes AttributeError on .upper()
src/forms.py:33 important - valid_form_methods mutable class list; use tuple
tests/test_forms.py:23 nit - parametrize reads mutable list, order-fragile
tests/test_forms.py:29 nit - no test covers method=None
votes.evidence_quote: `kwargs.pop("method", form.method).upper()` raises `AttributeError` when the caller passes `method=None` explicitly, because `None.upper()` is invalid.
votes.justification: The first finding names the exact line in from_form and the AttributeError on an explicit method=None. It also notes that the parent Request handles None, so None should be accepted, which matches the known defect.
